sources_considered.why: Reports that Amazon takes NVIDIA racks before power is ready; shows some sales come before use.
Reports CoreWeave's short install times, which bear on typical lags.
Summarizes Morgan Stanley's 32 GW power-gap forecast, but the page shows no publication date, and it is a forecast, not deployment data.

receipt.public_excerpt: Some AWS facilities reportedly had physical space for additional racks but lacked sufficient power infrastructure to activate them, leading Amazon to stage equipment in intermediary warehouses until sites were ready.

evidence_items.explanation: Shows that some 2026 NVIDIA purchases at Amazon come before they can be powered. It gives no share of all sales and no length of delay.

receipt.public_excerpt: CoreWeave disclosed in May 2025 that its hardware goes through a “~3 month installation time” between delivery and monetization. By late 2025, this had decreased to “within weeks”.

evidence_items.explanation: For one major neocloud, the gap from delivery to use was weeks to months, not years. It is from 2025 and covers one buyer, so it does not settle 2026 sales overall.

receipt.public_excerpt: Whether the warehoused hardware proves prescient or premature depends on how fast power infrastructure and construction can close the gap.

evidence_items.explanation: Shows that how long warehoused hardware will wait is still unknown, which is the gap that keeps this claim open.

unresolved_gaps: No public data matches 2026 NVIDIA or Broadcom chip sales to install dates.
